program: Housing-policy research, education, coalition support and Metropolitan Abundance Project

what: California YIMBY Education Fund produces housing research and implementation analysis and supports the national Metropolitan Abundance Project.
It is legally distinct from California YIMBY's advocacy and political entities.
The conditional estimate prices a California housing-health component against all recipient spending; other geographic and policy benefits remain unpriced.
strengths: A plausible high-leverage pathway runs from better implementation rules to additional homes, lower housing costs and improved living conditions.
Original research discusses financial feasibility and local implementation, not merely legal zoning capacity.
Independent empirical supply research supports an affordability mechanism, while the report keeps that distinct from health outcomes.
reservations: No reviewed source identifies the marginal extra completed homes caused by an ordinary Education Fund donation.
California benefit allocation is not the same as its Sacramento address: MAP explicitly works nationally and the c4 shares employees.
The accounts change from cash in 2022–23 to accrual in 2024, and housing or financial gains cannot automatically be priced as QALYs.

sections.what: The [recipient's research catalogue](https://cayimby.org/reports/) covers ADU implementation, housing impact fees, underproduction and local approval processes. Its [national MAP project](https://www.metroabundance.org/about-us/) works on housing, transportation and governance; MAP's [giving page](https://www.metroabundance.org/donate/) identifies the Education Fund as its recipient. The main [giving instructions](https://cayimby.org/waystogive/) distinguish this c3 from California YIMBY's c4 and PAC. Shared branding does not justify assigning every affiliate policy win to this charitable gift.
sections.monitoring: The [ADU retrospective](https://cayimby.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/CAY-ADU_Report-2024-v4.pdf) documents a substantial permitting expansion but is a historical, uncontrolled policy account, not a marginal donor evaluation. Its chart separates permits from completions; footnotes note changing data collection and unverified affordability classifications. No new gift receives credit for all past ADUs. A useful next evaluation would link a specific Education Fund analysis or implementation intervention to changed rules, actual net completions, occupancy, resident outcomes and a credible no-intervention comparison.
sections.qualitative:
[Research on large new apartments](https://research.upjohn.org/up_workingpapers/316/) supports rent reductions nearby rather than inevitable rent inflation, but is not a health trial and may not transfer to small ADUs or every neighborhood. [Terner's early SB9 review](https://ternercenter.berkeley.edu/research-and-policy/sb-9-turns-one-applications/) shows why legal or modeled feasible capacity is not production: financing, local restrictions and construction constraints matter. [HCD's current SB79 guidance](https://www.hcd.ca.gov/planning-and-research/sb79-tod) confirms the law is already operative and public agencies have implementation duties; future gifts need to improve on that funded baseline. Housing can affect health through stability, crowding, location and pollution, but [MTO](https://www.nber.org/papers/w18772) concerns a different low-income mobility intervention with heterogeneous effects. The [recent income trial](https://www.nber.org/papers/w32711) also cautions against treating financial relief as an automatic lasting clinical gain.

Affordability can change disposable resources independently of health; housingsecurity welfare overlaps clinicalutility. Net genuine rent/pay/commute changes jointly aftertax/benefitwithdrawal, preserve allnegative costs and distinguish renter gains from owner/public incidence. Do not attribute existing completed homes or affiliated politicalwins to a new c3gift.

Resource equivalents are welfare comparisons, not measured clinicalQALYs. Original health-only$454.77million and all original worlds remain diagnostics. This is partial occupant incidence, not global netresource creation or a complete policyportfolio return.

The original clinical calculation below remains the health-only diagnostic, not the current signed headline.

The conditional California housing-health price is $454.77 million per ten California QALYs. It charges three years of all recipient spending, $9,141,486, including national and unpriced activities. It is not a complete portfolio or societal return. We posit 1,000 net additional occupied California homes conditional on an implementation change over that support window; this is an explicit scale judgment, not permitted capacity, a project pipeline or a forecast from the ADU report.

A 10% incremental coalition implementation probability, 10% Education Fund contribution and 25% ordinary-funding response imply 2.5 net additional home-equivalents. The c3 contribution excludes credit assigned to its c4 and public agencies. Ten years of benefit at years 3–12 gives 8.040534 discounted home-years per added home. A judgmental 0.01 QALY per home-year across affected residents yields 0.201013 California QALYs, without multiplying again by household occupancy. The utility prior is not inferred from rent dollars, the MTO trial or a housing unit count.

Net homes exclude displacement of construction elsewhere in California. Health may arise through less harmful crowding or instability, but some residents simply move from other adequate housing, and transportation or pollution effects can offset gains. Current SB79 duties and already permitted development are baseline. A construction-resource sensitivity adds $500,000 per attributable net home; this is a judgmental resource proxy, not a current local unit quote or net fiscal cost.

Fresh giving instructions retain the separate c3EducationFund,EIN85-1438188, distinct from c4/PAC. The2024fees research discusses constructionfeasibility, affordability and municipal revenueincidence; its unitcost/assetvalue claims are not gift-caused householdincome. Existing operative housinglaws and publicimplementation duties, permittedpipelines, finance and otheradvocates remain baseline. [Giving](https://cayimby.org/waystogive/) [Historicalfee research](https://cayimby.org/reports/the-impact-of-fees/)

The resource cohort is the same2.5conditional net additional occupied California home-equivalents, with one household-equivalent per unit as an explicit distribution judgment, not observed clients or an extra residentmultiplier. Changing occupants, renter/owner mix and continuity are unknown; tenfinitehome-years atyears3–12use the original8.040534discountedyears. No clinicalutility coefficient discounts householdburdens. Three-year fullcost and100,000gift-window scaling use the same reach boundary, with fundingresponse once.

The illustrative central assigns50%of households$1200annual genuine rent/payment/commute-spending reduction, retains80%after taxes, benefitwithdrawal and substitution, then discounts positivevalue50%for housingsecurity/health overlap. Every household incurs FULL$100annual incremental unreimbursed household commute/admin/opportunity loss, disjoint from recipient/provider/construction/infrastructure resources already priced. At a hypothetical$30,000annual resourcebaseline, jointgroups therefore net+$380and−$100; separate0.5timeshouseholds timesdiscountedyears timeslog(1+net/baseline). These dollar/share amounts are unmeasured judgments, not observedrentcuts or productivejob earnings. No asset appreciation, housingretailvalue, grosssalary or ordinarysurvivorwages is counted.

Financialnull/unknown, clinicalnull/financial-only, zeroimplementation/funding, no rentsaving, adversecommute andzero-positive-overlap worlds retain fullnegative burdens. Rent reductions can transfer resources from landlords: a disjointlandlord-consumption loss world exposes that incidence rather than claiming universal netgain. Publicpayer loss and additional$500,000perattributablehome realconstructionresources are distinct alternatives, not duplicate transfers, and capitalresidualvalue remainsunmeasured. Broader nearbyrent, jobs, ownerwealth, transportation andnationalMAP effects remainunknown, not zero.
sections.funding:
The [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/851438188/202523219349314572/full) reports $3,047,162 expenses and $1,628,879 revenue, with $4,318,400 unrestricted and $845,879 restricted net assets. Spending is $2,833,521 program, $150,595 management and $63,046 fundraising. [Schedule R](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349314572/IRS990ScheduleR) identifies shared employees with the c4; [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202523219349314572/IRS990ScheduleD) records $386,898 due to a related party. Original [2022](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/851438188/202410339349301631/full) and [2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/851438188/202403189349309890/full) returns check cash accounting, while 2024 checks accrual. The displayed historical series is therefore not a clean three-year mean. A deficit supports asking about future capacity, but neither it nor reserves establishes the effect of a marginal gift. Construction capital, public infrastructure and costs to other advocates are outside the recipient denominator and must be disclosed in any future societal comparison.

Fresh checks of all three original returns confirm no separately netted event or inventory costs. The 2024 accrual versus 2022–23 cash distinction remains; no synthetic comparable mean is produced. The 2024 and 2023 Schedule D expense-reconciliation sections are blank, not evidence of zero donated services; the 2022 Schedule D endpoint was unavailable. Unrecognized shared or volunteer resources remain a cost limitation. The c3-specific source perimeter is retained.

model.costScope: Three years of whole-recipient FY2024 accrual cost, including national MAP and support functions. Partial California housing-health estimate. Private construction, public infrastructure and unrecognized shared/volunteer resources not in central donor cost; sensitivity added. Household burden excludes reimbursed recipient/construction/infrastructure costs already priced. Rent savings are occupant incidence, not global net resource creation; disjoint landlord/public consumption and realconstructioncost alternatives expose scope.
model.geographicAttribution: N explicitly counts net additional occupied California homes, not all national MAP output. u is total California resident health per net home-year and includes occupancy/displacement within its subjective value; no population or household multiplier. The home-year utility is an expected net health area across changing occupants and already includes survival, occupancy turnover and benefit fade by judgment; it is not a fixed utility promised to every initial resident for ten years.
model.formula: C=3*E; U=N*p*a*b; A=sum_{t=3}^{12}(1+d)^(-t); Q_CA=U*A*u. P10=10*C/Q_CA. Only ten finite home-years; N net of replacement/displaced construction. Resource stress C'=C+U*500000. Other health remains unknown. Resource household-equivalents=U, no occupancy/clinicalutility multiplier. Joint renter-saving/non-saving netresources afterretention and positiveoverlap minusFULLburden; .5*people*A*log1p(net/baseline), years3–12 matchclinicalhorizon. Three-year100000gift changesE=100000/3 and reachproportionally.
model.counterfactual: SB79 is operative, HCD and local governments have statutory duties, existing finance/building pipelines and other advocates continue. Credit only additional completed occupied homes beyond these and net of construction elsewhere, not all newly legal capacity.
model.attribution: p incremental coalition implementation, a c3 Education Fund contribution distinct from c4/shared staff, b gift funding response; each once. Conditional N is before those factors, not a donor-attributable forecast.
model.uncertainty: N, policy probabilities and health conversion are uncalibrated judgments. Large price range does not validate any particular yield. Financial relief and mobility trials do not establish health per market-rate home. Whole portfolio remains unpriced. Householduniqueequivalence, renter/owner mix, netprivatepayment reduction, retention, overlap and burden are unmeasured hypotheses. Nearby marketrents, productivejobs, ownerlandvalue and nationalMAPresource effects unknown.
